title: Eni Working With Venezuela to Revive Energy Sector Amid US Push
summary: Eni SpA said it’s working with Venezuelan authorities to help revive the country’s energy sector, as the US moves to secure greater control over its vast oil industry.

title: Iceland Rejects Restarting EU Membership Talks
summary: Icelandic voters rejected restarting EU accession talks, with opposition particularly strong outside Reykjavik as concerns over sovereignty, fisheries and agriculture outweighed arguments for closer European ties.  RÚV Iceland News Defense & Security Correspondent Ingólfur Sigfússon is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says says the result puts membership talks on hold and could shift attention toward Norway as Nordic countries reassess their relationships with Europe amid geopolitical uncertainty. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Dollar Debasement Backs Bull Case for Emerging Bonds, Funds Say
summary: A stellar year for emerging-market bonds is set to get even better as the return of the “dollar debasement trade” amplifies inflows into the asset class, fund managers say.

title: NASA’s Roman Telescope Takes Aim at Cosmic Mysteries
summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy on a mission to study dark energy, dark matter and planets beyond our solar system. Roman is headed about 1 million miles from Earth to Lagrange point 2, where its wide field of view will allow scientists to survey billions of galaxies far faster than the Hubble telescope. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend to watch the launch with hosts Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz is Space Network Co-Founder and COO Ross Hamilton to discuss the telescope's mission. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Chinese Solar Giant Longi Reports Deeper Net Loss in First Half
summary: Longi Green Energy Technology Co. joined other Chinese solar producers in reporting a first-half loss that widened from a year earlier, underscoring a downturn in the sector that has lasted for more than two years.

title: Inside the Dangote Family: Core Lessons from Africa's Richest Man
summary: Aliko Dangote's daughters share the core life and leadership lessons learned from their father. They reflect on his teachings about humility, hard work, persistence, and his strong belief in the vital role of women in leadership. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Day Traders Are Abandoning Korean Chip Leveraged ETFs in Droves
summary: An onerous mock trading course is becoming an effective tool for South Korea to cool investor fervor over risky products that have turned the country’s $4.3 trillion stock market extremely volatile.

title: Guggenheim Ties Weigh on Acrisure Debt, Dragging High-Yield Credit Markets
summary: It had already been a tough 2026 for Acrisure. Part fintech, part insurance broker, the firm said in late May it would cut 11% of its workforce, or some 2,250 people, as part of a sweeping overhaul to modernize operations. Some of its bonds and loans had fallen, but still remained above levels typically deemed distressed.

title: Warsh Says Inflation Isn’t Slowing, Vows to Reach 2% Target
summary: Warsh reiterated that policymakers have a "firm, fixed target" of 2% inflation at the 2026 Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium. Bloomberg's Maria Eloisa Capurro explains.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Supercars Fuel a New Hybrid Boom
summary: Hybrids are enjoying a resurgence as slower EV adoption and continued demand for combustion engines reshape the auto industry, with the technology increasingly appearing in high-performance and luxury cars. Co-host of Bloomberg's "Hot Pursuit!" Hannah Elliott explains to Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz why brands including Audi, Lamborghini, Ferrari and Bugatti are using electric motors to boost performance while preserving the sound and feel buyers still want from combustion engines. Watch, on Bloomberg This Weekend. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: A $2,000 Sweater Reveals Fashion’s True Cost
summary: Content creator Macy Gilliam spent 90-hours over four months and about $2,000 making a sweater from scratch, starting with wool from a sheep at New York City’s Queens County Farm Museum. Gilliam joins Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend where she explains that the project gave her a new appreciation for the labor behind clothing and raised questions about transparency, quality and ethics across fashion’s complex supply chains.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Warsh Sets the Tone for Fed’s Road Ahead
summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s first Jackson Hole speech gave central bankers and investors greater clarity on how he views the economy and the Fed’s path ahead, though questions remain about the timing and number of potential rate hikes. Bloomberg Odd Lots co-host Joe Weisenthal is on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss the annual gathering, where monetary policy debates mix with informal conversations among some of the world’s most influential central bankers.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Can the US Defy Fiscal Gravity?
summary: David Bianco of DWS says long-term Treasury yields and real rates have climbed to some of their highest levels in nearly 25 years, but he argues inflation is not the main driver. The bigger issues are structural: US deficits above 6% of GDP, a rising total debt-to-GDP ratio, and the need to fund more borrowing domestically as foreign demand becomes less reliable. The US still benefits from the dollar’s safe-haven status, but Robin Brooks of the Brookings Institution and former Dutch Finance Minister Sigrid Kaag warn that America’s fiscal path remains dangerous even if its “exorbitant privilege” gives policymakers more time before markets force discipline.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: $700 Cash Grants Transform Lives in Malawi
summary: The nonprofit GiveDirectly, with a large backing from Canva, is providing eligible adults in two Malawi districts with about $700 each, roughly equivalent to the country’s annual income per person, with virtually no restrictions on how the money is spent. Bloomberg News Senior Africa Reporter Antony Sguazzin joins Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz on Bloomberg This Weekend and reports recipients are investing in businesses, livestock and home improvements, offering a test of whether large-scale direct cash transfers can provide a more efficient model for development aid. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Russia Tests Ukraine and NATO With Escalation
summary: Russia is intensifying missile and drone attacks on Ukraine as Kyiv faces shortages of Patriot interceptors, raising concerns about its ability to defend against ballistic missiles heading into winter. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend are Bloomberg Economics Geoeconomics Analyst Alex Kokcharov and Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Defense Analyst Col. Wayne Sanders who discuss Russia’s hybrid attacks against NATO members and the challenge of building cheaper defenses against increasingly sophisticated drone warfare. (Source: Bloomberg)
